meta.description: Artemis candidate landing regions (13 of Aug 2022, 9 of Oct 2024), the Moon Base / Shackleton Connecting Ridge site, and literature point sites near the lunar south pole. Values copied from research notes.
meta.coordinate_convention: Decimal degrees; latitude south negative; longitude east-positive, given as lon_east_180 (-180..180) and lon_east_360 (0..360). Trek polygons are south polar stereographic metres (R = 1,737,400 m, +y toward lon 0, +x toward 90 E).
notes: Values copied from research notes of 2026-11-14; not independently validated.

NASA has published NO official centre coordinates or boundary files for either the 13 (2022) or the 9 (2024) regions. Top-level lat/lon of a region is the LROC NAC mosaic centre where one exists (LROC team product, Henriksen et al. 2023; absolute positional accuracy 5-20 m, 1 m/px), otherwise the centre computed by the researcher from the NASA Trek 2022 polygon. Both are kept; see alt_coordinates.

LROC mosaic footprints are larger than NASA's ~15 x 15 km boxes (researcher-computed N-S extents: Malapert ~21 km, Faustini Rim A ~20 km, Peak near Shackleton ~22 km, Peak near Cabeus B and Amundsen Rim ~26 km, Nobile Rim 2 ~27 km, de Gerlache Rim ~37 km, Haworth ~39 km, Mons Mouton Plateau ~88 km). Treat centres as approximate region positions, not official NASA centres.

Trek polygon centres were computed by the researcher with the spherical polar stereographic inverse (lat = -90 + 2*atan(rho/(2R)), lon = atan2(x, y)); they are derived values, not NASA-published. The 0..360 form of Trek longitudes was added during conversion (value + 360 where negative). Notes call the Trek boxes 'schematic region boxes rather than surveyed boundaries'.
Size conflict kept: NASA release says each region is about 15 x 15 km; Trek boxes are 16-30 km on a side.

Mapping of LROC mosaic names to region names (e.g. 2024 'Mons Mouton' -> 'Nobile Rim 1 and Mons Mouton (Leibnitz Beta Plateau)' mosaic; 'de Gerlache Rim 2' -> single 'de Gerlache Rim' mosaic) is the researcher's reading of product titles, not a NASA statement.

No list for Artemis IV has been published; per NASA (LPSC 2026) the nine regions are specific to Artemis III and do not constrain Artemis IV and later. As of Oct-Nov 2026 the site of the first crewed landing (now Artemis IV) is undecided.
Wueller et al. 2026 (JGR Planets, doi 10.1029/2025JE009434) Table A1 lists 130 candidate landing sites with coordinates but could not be retrieved (HTTP 403); those sites are NOT in this file.
source_url may be a string or an array of strings.

general_selection_criteria.2022_release: Terrain slope, ease of communications with Earth, lighting conditions; launch-window availability (several regions so launches are possible throughout the year); combined capabilities of SLS, Orion and Starship HLS; proximity to PSRs for a moonwalk; all 13 regions contain sites with continuous sunlight throughout a 6.5-day surface stay; each region ~15 x 15 km; landing site = ~100 m radius; all within 6 deg latitude of the pole.
general_selection_criteria.2024_release: Science potential, launch window availability, terrain suitability, communication capabilities with Earth, lighting conditions, combined trajectory capabilities of SLS, Orion and Starship HLS; no priority order; no sizes or coordinates given.
general_selection_criteria.lpsc2026_downselection: End-to-end mission availability evaluated on a calendar basis; NRHO assumed (SUPERSEDED Oct 2026); surface stay ~5.75-6.25 days; minimise slope variability in landing ellipse; hazards (craters, blocks, rough terrain); greater Earth visibility preferred if DTE; illumination for whole stay, shifting ~2-3 weeks per year; regions robust across epochs favoured; removed regions are not unsuitable for later missions.

items.name: Moon Base I landing target: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
items.selection_criteria_notes: NASA (26 May 2026, as quoted): Moon Base I (Blue Moon MK1 'Endurance') 'will land on the Shackleton Connecting Ridge to demonstrate capabilities that reduce risk for future crewed Artemis landing missions in 2028'. The Moon Base is 'located at the lunar South Pole'; base location to be confirmed from Phase 1 robotic scouting; Phase 2 speaks of multiple locations. Reporting rationale: near-continuous solar power on sunlit ridges, water ice in nearby PSRs. NASA 2022: ridge 'could have ice below the surface'. One outlet (TechTimes) claims the plan 'locks' Shackleton crater rim by 2036 - single secondary source, not stated by NASA.
items.evidence: NASA statement via secondary quotation; fixed base site NOT established
items.caveat: No coordinates for the Moon Base I landing target were published. For approximate ridge positions see connecting_ridge (Trek-derived), connecting_ridge_shackleton_junction and illumination_sites.json.
